title: Reliability dependency & decision matrix - sprint template
summary: A compact working template for mapping cross-functional dependencies, scoring risk, and making go/no-go decisions during SLO rollouts. Designed to be used as the working agenda and artifact during a 4-week rollout sprint with product, infra, and support leads.
content:
Purpose
This doc is a lightweight, shareable artifact to: 1) capture upstream/downstream dependencies for any new or revised SLO, 2) present a simple decision matrix for canary -> canary+ -> global rollout gates, and 3) provide a week-by-week sprint checklist for cross-functional teams to coordinate the rollout.

Scope
- Target: service-level SLOs (latency and availability) for API surfaces provided by the serving runtime and control plane.
- Not covered: billing model changes, pricing tiers, or long-term infra capacity contracts (those get separate tracks).

How to use this template
1) Fill in the service stub below. 2) Run the dependency interview with each stakeholder (15–30m each) and capture blockers. 3) Complete the risk score and decide the initial canary % and telemetry windows. 4) Use the week-by-week checklist during the sprint and annotate the decisions in the matrix.

Service stub
- Service name: <service-name>
- Owner: <team / person>
- SLO target(s): e.g., p95 latency < 120ms; availability 99.95% monthly
- Stakeholder contact list: product, infra, devex, observability, customer-success, legal (if customer-impacting)

Dependency map (fill during interviews)
- Dependency: e.g., shared KV cache layer
  - Owner: infra-shared-services
  - Type: blocking / soft / informational
  - Expected completion date or mitigation: 
  - Notes: e.g., cache TTL changes may invalidate prefix cache assumptions

Decision matrix (scoring guide)
Columns: Item | Impact if Fails | Likelihood | Detectability | Risk score (I*L*D) | Mitigation / Contingency
- Impact if Fails: 1 low - 5 catastrophic
- Likelihood: 1 rare - 5 very likely
- Detectability: 1 easy to detect - 5 hard to detect
- Suggested thresholds: Risk score 1–9 => green, 10–49 => amber, >=50 => red

Example row:
- KV cache dependency | Impact 4 | Likelihood 3 | Detectability 2 | Score 24 | Mitigation: enable read-through fallback to DB + monitor cache miss surge metric

Rollout gating rules (recommended)
- Canary: 1–2% traffic to canary nodes for 48 hours; required telemetry pass: no new p95 regressions > 10% and no customer-facing errors > 1/hour.
- Canary+: 5–10% traffic for 72 hours; required telemetry pass: steady state p95 within 7% of baseline and error rate within SLA budget.
- Global: progressive ramp to 100% over 3 days with abort window at any significant anomaly.

Telemetry & validation checklist (concrete queries to add to dashboards)
- Latency distribution by endpoint and client (p50/p95/p99)
- Error rate by endpoint (5xxs, throttles) and by route tag (internal / external)
- Request volume by customer tier and model variant
- Backend saturation metrics: GPU utilization, queue depth, KV cache miss rate
- End-to-end user-visible errors (customer 1st-party): count and sample traces
- Regression detection rule examples: detect p95 increase > 10% vs baseline over rolling 60m window

Suggested alert thresholds (start conservative, tune during canary)
- Latency p95 > target * 1.2 for 15m => P2 (investigate)
- Error rate > 0.5% for external API endpoints for 10m => P1 if sustained and customer impact confirmed
- Backend queue depth > 75th percentile historical peak for 5m => P1 (capacity stress)

Communications & stakeholder cadence
- Weekly SRE x Product sync (30m): status, top blockers, dependency changes.
- Twice-daily canary standup (15m) during active canary days: owner updates + immediate roll/abort vote. Attendees: SRE oncall lead, product PM, infra lead, observability engineer, customer-success standby.
- Post-mortem / playback within 3 business days after any abort or incident during rollout.

Week-by-week sprint template (4 weeks)
- Week 0 (prep, pre-sprint): finalize SLO definition, run dependency interviews, baseline metrics captured, add telemetry queries to dashboards.
- Week 1 (canary): deploy canary subset; observe 48–72h; run canary standups; checklist: verify telemetry ingestion, smoke tests, sample traces pulled.
- Week 2 (canary+ / scale tests): expand to 5–10% and run synthetic load tests that mimic high fanout and long sequences; confirm mitigations hold under load.
- Week 3 (progressive ramp): staged traffic increases, monitor for throttling, latency drift, and cost anomalies; finalize rollout communications.
- Week 4 (stabilize & retro): full ramp if cleared, otherwise rollback and re-plan. Run retro and update runbooks/alerts.

Runbook anchors to prepare (pull into service runbooks)
- How to revert a config-only rollout (feature flags, routing policies)
- How to drain canary nodes and re-route traffic back to stable pool
- Quick rollback play: steps to disable model variant or quantization profile if causing regressions
- Triage checklist for P1 during rollout (who does what in first 15m, first hour)

Risk scoring rubric (quick)
- Score 1–9 green: proceed with standard canary
- Score 10–49 amber: require additional mitigation (integration testing, longer canary)
- Score >=50 red: do not proceed until mitigations complete

Open questions to answer in first stakeholder sync
- Which customers should be excluded from canary traffic? (enterprise customers with SLAs?)
- Are there any compliance or data residency flags for this rollout?
- Does the canary path touch any experimental kernels or quantization that could affect outputs?

Decision record template (copy into the rollout ticket)
- Date: YYYY-MM-DD
- Decision by: names / roles (SRE lead, product PM, infra lead)
- Decision: go / pause / abort / rollback
- Rationale: short justification and risk notes
- Action items (owners + due dates)

Archive & post-rollout hygiene
- Update the SLO ownership matrix with the final owner and runbook links.
- Add any new dashboard panels to the global SRE SLO dashboard.
- Capture lessons learned in a 15–30m playback and attach to the ticket.

Appendix: quick checklist you can copy into a ticket
- [ ] Baseline metrics captured and saved
- [ ] Dependencies interviewed and scored
- [ ] Canary deployment plan documented (traffic %, nodes, duration)
- [ ] Telemetry queries added to dashboard + alert rules staged
- [ ] Standby rotation assigned for canary days
- [ ] Communication plan and customer exclusion list confirmed
- [ ] Rollback steps documented and rehearsed

Notes & drafting history
- Drafted by Jordan Patel as a working template for SRE -> product rollout collaboration.
- Intends to be minimal and pragmatic: copy into a JIRA ticket, iterate with stakeholders.
- Next: run this template on upcoming model-quantization SLO change and capture feedback.
